members.label: Team members
members.doc: One row per person, in the order they appear on the page. Drag to reorder. Until the first row is added the page keeps the nine placeholder cards it shows today.

photo.label: Headshot
photo.doc: Fills the card. Square or portrait crops sit best. No photo yet is fine — the card falls back to its color block.

photo_tone.label: Headshot — color
photo_tone.doc: Color is the default. Switch this photo to black and white when you want it that way on purpose — the photography on this site was only ever gray because the placeholder images were. Affects this photo alone.

photo_px.label: Headshot — movement
photo_px.doc: How far this photo drifts inside its frame as you scroll, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off. The dropdown this replaces offered 6, 10 and 16 as Subtle, Medium and Strong, so anything already set still reads exactly the same — you can now pick the values in between. 40 is the ceiling: the page itself stops there, so a larger number would do nothing. The photo is laid out taller than its frame and slides within it, so an edge never appears and it is never zoomed.

photo_px_dir.label: Headshot — movement direction
photo_px_dir.doc: Which way this photo travels as the page scrolls. Neighboring photos set in opposite directions are what reads as depth.

photo_float.label: Headshot — frame drift
photo_float.doc: Moves the whole frame across the section, on top of the movement inside it, as a percentage of the frame's height. 0 is off; 8 and 12 were the old Gentle and Strong. 40 is the ceiling. Leave this off for a photo that fills its section edge to edge — there is nothing behind it to reveal.

photo_float_dir.label: Headshot — drift direction
photo_float_dir.doc: Which way this frame drifts. Set a large and a small photo in opposite directions.

quote.label: Quote
quote.doc: Optional, shown under the card. Leave blank for none.

bg_color.label: Background color
bg_color.doc: The color behind this person's cut-out. Leave on Automatic and the grid cycles through the brand colors by position, so adding or removing someone re-colors the rest on its own. Pick a specific color only when you want to override that.

crop.label: Crop
crop.doc: Which part of the photo to keep when it does not fit the box exactly. With Fit the height this moves the person left or right; with Fill the box it also decides which edges are trimmed. Bottom is usually right for a cut-out, so they stand on the base of the box.

choices.bottom: Bottom — stands on the base of the box

overflow.label: Let the photo hang outside the box
overflow.doc: Normally the photo is trimmed at the edges of the colored box. Switch this on and anything wider than the box shows outside it — useful when something should break out of the frame, like a raised arm or a prop. Only does anything when How the photos fit is set to Fit the height; the other two settings always resolve inside the box.

choices.hidden: No — trim it at the edges

hovercrop.label: Keep this photo inside the box on hover
hovercrop.doc: When someone hovers a card the photo normally lifts and the top of the head rises out of the colored box. Switch this on for a photo that is already cut off at the top — lifting it would only show the flat edge of the crop. The card still reacts: the color still shrinks and the photo still scales, it just stays inside the box.

choices.free: No — let the top lift out of the box

card_shape.label: Card shape
card_shape.doc: The shape of every photo box in the grid. This is one setting for the whole grid on purpose — a grid of mixed shapes reads as a mistake rather than a choice. Use the crop on each person to deal with how they sit inside it.

photo_fit.label: How the photos fit
photo_fit.doc: How each cut-out sits in its box. Fit the height pins the photo to the full height of the box so everyone matches, and lets the width fall where it does — that is the setting the design is built around. Fill the box crops whichever edge is too big. Show the whole photo never crops, but people end up different sizes.

choices.height: Fit the height — everyone the same height, sides may crop
choices.cover: Fill the box — crops whichever edges overflow
choices.contain: Show the whole photo — nothing cropped, gaps at the sides

columns.label: Columns on a wide screen
columns.doc: How many people sit side by side on a desktop screen. Narrower screens step down on their own — two across on a tablet, one on a phone — so this is only the widest case. Four needs a genuinely wide window to be worth it; below about 1240px it falls back to three so the cards do not get too small for a face.

quote_mark.label: Quote mark behind the quote
quote_mark.doc: A large quotation mark sitting behind each person's quote. Matching the card color keeps it quiet — it reads as texture rather than an element. Yellow is louder and the same on every card. Either way it only appears where a quote has been written.

choices.match: Match each person's card color — subtle
choices.yellow: Yellow — bolder, same on every card

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.
